correctness.rationale: The real balancing lemma is self-contained and the two field-sensitive non-trace-class cases were checked explicitly: symmetric non-trace-class compression is balanced by bounded real 2x2 similarities, while a non-trace-class skew-adjoint part is balanced by fixed real shears. Trace-class perturbations contribute only l1 diagonals. Tran's dimension-free theorem supplies the same-field finite-matrix commutator input needed by Liu's zero-diagonal and gluing constructions; the remaining Sylvester, block, tensor, and similarity operations preserve the real field.

originality.rationale: Liu's 2026 theorem is explicitly stated for complex Hilbert space, while Tran's 2026 same-field theorem is finite-dimensional. Exact and synonymous searches for the real infinite-dimensional compact single-commutator statement, plus current SCOPE overlap searches, found no coverage. Anderson's rank-one construction and classical zero-diagonal methods are treated as prior art. Full-text access to several older diagonal/commutator papers was incomplete, so the claim remains to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result closes the real-field analogue of the newly solved compact Pearcy--Topping problem, preserves a universal square-root norm bound, and isolates a reusable real diagonal-balancing mechanism that avoids the complex four-phase step. Complexification alone does not give a single real commutator, so the field-preserving argument is substantive.
